skill.name: use-my-browser
skill.description: Guides agents in choosing public web reads, raw fetches, live Chrome DevTools, or clean browser automation for browser-focused tasks.
skill.summary: Choose the least intrusive browser path for web research, DevTools handoff, and live session work.
skill.author: xixu-me

security_audit.summary: Static alerts were mostly false positives caused by Markdown inline code, browser tool names, and a Chinese translation file. The real risk is contextual: the skill intentionally guides access to live authenticated browser sessions, DevTools inspection, page script evaluation, and raw fetch workflows.

remediation.issue: Live browser access can expose authenticated user data.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent language before using signed-in pages, selected DevTools requests, cookies, or open tabs.

remediation.issue: DevTools script evaluation and raw fetches are powerful inspection paths.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that evaluate_script, network reads, raw fetches, and uploads should be limited to the stated user goal.

remediation.issue: Remote debugging configuration can be risky on a normal browser profile.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the guidance against unnecessary remote debugging prominent, and prefer safer auto-connect flows when available.

remediation.issue: The skill references a session playbook file that is not present in the package.
remediation.suggestion: Add the referenced file or remove the links so safety guidance is not missing at runtime.

content.value_statement: Web tasks often need different access paths, from public sources to signed-in browser sessions. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code choose the least intrusive workflow.
actual_capabilities: Routes tasks between public web tools, raw fetches, Chrome DevTools, and clean browser contexts.
Guides safe use of logged-in Chrome state when cookies or current app context matter.
Explains DOM snapshots, selected network requests, console messages, screenshots, and performance evidence.
Supports DevTools handoff from selected elements or highlighted requests.
Stores reusable site notes for confirmed URL patterns, login needs, extraction tactics, and known traps.
limitations: It is a strategy skill, not a standalone browser automation runtime.
Live session work needs Chrome DevTools, web, shell, or browser tools in the host environment.
Authenticated access can expose sensitive pages, requests, cookies, and user data.
It does not guarantee access to private, anti-bot-heavy, or rapidly changing sites.

use_cases.title: Debug a Signed-In Web App
use_cases.description: Inspect current page state, selected requests, console errors, and rendering issues without recreating the session.

use_cases.title: Research Dynamic Public Pages
use_cases.description: Start with public sources, then use browser inspection when static reads miss rendered content.

use_cases.title: Extract Real Page Assets
use_cases.description: Find image, video, or metadata sources from lazy-loaded pages with minimal browser disruption.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Browser Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the browser strategy for this page task. First choose public web, raw fetch, live Chrome DevTools, or a clean browser context.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect My Current Tab
prompt_templates.prompt: I have the relevant page open in Chrome. Use the live browser only as needed, preserve my tab state, and explain the evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Selected Request
prompt_templates.prompt: I selected a failing request in DevTools. Inspect that request first, then compare nearby network activity only if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Several Sites
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these sites with the cheapest reliable layer for each one. Batch public research, and use browser inspection only for dynamic evidence.

output_examples.input: Check whether this dashboard bug is caused by the frontend or the API.
output_examples.output: The agent starts from the signed-in tab, checks the selected request and console output, then reports the failing endpoint and UI symptom.

output_examples.input: Find the real video URL from this lazy-loaded article page.
output_examples.output: The agent reads page structure first, inspects media elements and requests, then reports the discovered asset source.

output_examples.input: Compare three public product pages and cite the sources.
output_examples.output: The agent begins with public reads, opens a browser only for rendered pages, and returns a concise source-backed comparison.

best_practices: Define the success condition before choosing public web, raw fetch, live browser, or clean browser tooling.
Use the least intrusive layer that can answer the question, and escalate only when evidence requires it.
Protect the user session by avoiding unrelated tabs, destructive actions, and unnecessary browser interaction.
anti_patterns: Opening or modifying the user browser when public sources already answer the request.
Treating screenshots or not-found pages as final evidence before checking DOM, network, or source data.
Using raw fetches, DevTools scripts, or file uploads without confirming the goal and user intent.

faq.question: Does this skill control my browser by itself?
faq.answer: No. It gives routing and safety guidance for agents that already have browser, web, shell, or DevTools tools.

faq.question: When should an agent use the live Chrome session?
faq.answer: Use it when the task depends on login state, cookies, current app context, selected DevTools data, or rendered behavior.

faq.question: Can it work without Chrome DevTools MCP?
faq.answer: Public research and raw fetch workflows can still apply, but live-session handoff needs browser tooling.

faq.question: How does it reduce risk?
faq.answer: It tells the agent to start with lower-risk reads and protect the current browser session during escalation.

faq.question: Can it inspect private or signed-in pages?
faq.answer: Yes, if the user grants access through the current browser session. This can expose sensitive data.

faq.question: Is this mainly for research or debugging?
faq.answer: It supports both cited research and authenticated debugging, plus dynamic site inspection and DevTools handoff.
